transcript.content: Hello. I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

I can handle the technical parts of my job fine, but I just can’t seem to keep all the pieces of these projects organized anymore. Ever since I took on a lead role, managing all the different moving parts has become really overwhelming.
Have you struggled with organization and managing details throughout your life—such as during school or earlier in your career—or is this difficulty entirely new since taking on this lead role?

Looking back, this scattered feeling has actually been with me since primary school, when teachers would write "brilliant ideas but careless mistakes" on my report cards and my parents had to sit with me just to finish homework. I managed to get by earlier in my career, but it became completely unmanageable once I stepped into this lead architect role a year ago.

Besides feeling overwhelmed by work, do you find yourself constantly worrying about other areas of your life—like your health, family, or minor everyday matters—and is this worry difficult to control?

I don't really experience constant or uncontrollable worry about things like my health or family. Most of my stress and anxiety right now is tied directly to my struggles with managing my workload and my performance at my job.
Do these difficulties with organization, focus, or forgetfulness also affect your personal life, such as managing household chores, paying bills, or keeping track of appointments?

Yes, they definitely spill over—I’m constantly scrambling at the last minute with travel planning and gallery submissions for my art, and I'm always losing everyday things like my keys, work badge, or charger. While it's frustrating at home, my biggest worry is still how these slip-ups are affecting my performance and job security.
Do you often feel physically restless, find it hard to sit still, or tend to act or speak impulsively, both now and when you were a child?

I definitely feel a restless buzz during long meetings where I have to constantly shift or pace off-camera, and even sitting quietly to read or sketch makes me antsy. As for childhood, I was always scattered and made careless mistakes, but I don't recall being particularly impulsive back then.
When you were a child, did you have trouble staying seated in class, or did you often run around or climb on things excessively compared to other kids?
I don't really recall having those specific hyperactive behaviors like running around or climbing excessively when I was a kid. I was mostly just quiet and daydreaming at my desk.
When you were a child, did you often talk excessively, blurt out answers before a question was finished, or find it very difficult to wait your turn?

I don't recall having those specific issues like talking excessively or struggling to wait my turn when I was a child. My difficulties back then were really just about losing focus and making careless mistakes on my schoolwork.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a lifelong history of prominent inattentive symptoms, including chronic disorganization, careless mistakes, difficulty sustaining focus, and frequently losing essential items, dating back to primary school. While he reports mild physical restlessness in adulthood, he did not exhibit hyperactive or impulsive behaviors during childhood, aligning with a diagnosis of Attention Deficit Disorder without Hyperactivity (ICD-10: F98.8). These symptoms cause significant functional impairment in both his professional role as a lead architect and his personal life.
